# Solution Design: YouTube Input Normalization And Playback Controls
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent) on behalf of Agno JF

## Technical Approach

Use the existing Laravel modular monolith, Inertia React, TypeScript, and shadcn/ui baseline. Keep the existing `learning_sessions.video_url` column and normalize all accepted administrator input into a canonical YouTube watch URL before persistence.

## Input Normalization

The server-side parser accepts:

- `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID`
- `https://youtu.be/VIDEO_ID`
- `https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID`
- A complete iframe snippet whose `src` is one of the accepted YouTube URLs

The parser will:

1. Trim whitespace and decode HTML entities in pasted embed code.
2. Extract only the iframe `src` when HTML is supplied.
3. Allow only YouTube and YouTube privacy-enhanced hosts.
4. Extract one valid YouTube video ID.
5. Store `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID`.
6. Reject malformed IDs, unsupported hosts, and arbitrary HTML or script content.

The application never renders the pasted embed code directly.

## Generated Player

The server will generate a `youtube-nocookie.com` embed URL with:

```text
controls=0
rel=0
playsinline=1
iv_load_policy=3
enablejsapi=1
origin=<current application origin>
```

The player will use the YouTube IFrame API for an application-owned accessible control bar. The native YouTube controls remain disabled to reduce the visible `Watch on YouTube` path. The application controls will provide play or pause, seek, and mute actions.

The implementation will not rely on the deprecated `modestbranding` parameter, CSS overlays, or click interception as security controls.

## Server Security

- Keep `/classroom` and `/sessions/{learningSession}` inside the existing `auth` and `active` middleware group.
- Keep the published-session check in `LearningSessionController`.
- Return only the generated embed URL and required session display fields to participants.
- Do not return the original administrator input or render arbitrary HTML.
- Keep YouTube URL validation and normalization in server-side application code.

## Verification

- Feature tests cover URL, short URL, embed URL, and iframe-code submissions.
- Feature tests reject non-YouTube and malformed input.
- Feature tests cover the generated embed parameters and current origin.
- Existing authorization, published-session, resource-download, and revocation tests remain passing.
- Manual browser review must confirm the custom controls, responsive behavior, playback, and remaining browser-level URL discovery.

## Limitations

YouTube still receives the video ID in the browser. An authenticated participant can inspect the iframe or use browser tools to reconstruct the watch URL. This is an explicit residual limitation, not a failed claim of absolute protection.
